items.t: Обвал акций Nvidia оказывает давление на акции технологических компаний Гонконга, Hang Seng упал ниже 24 000 пунктов
sum: Tech majors were weighed down by news of Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia's chief executive last night, with Hong Kong shares opening down 136 points.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index fell 0.57 percent to 23,871 points, while the tech gauge dropped 0.35 percent to 3,918 points.
Tech heavyweights Alibaba (9988) and Tencent (0700) dipped 0.5 percent and 1.5 percent, respectively. Meituan (3690) declined 1.2 percent, and Xiaomi (1810) slipped 0.8 percent.

Local chipmakers rallied, with Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor gaining 2.79 percent as the best-performing blue chip, and Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (0981) rising 2.59 percent after announcing its interim results yesterday. The company's third-quarter revenue rose 6.1 percent year on year to US$3.19 billion (HK$24.88 billion), and it expects revenue to rise 4-6 percent in the fourth quarter.

Link Real Estate Investment (0823) contracted 1.7 percent after reassuring shareholders of a stable rental outlook in yesterday's interim results press conference, with its total distributable amount for the first half of the 2026/2027 financial year up 0.4 percent to HK$3.3 billion.

Oil prices rose sharply, with Brent futures settling up to US$3 per barrel as escalating Middle East conflict and attacks on energy infrastructure overshadowed rising crude output. CNOOC (0883) rose 0.8 percent, and PetroChina (0857) rose 0.6 percent.
Chinese commercial aerospace company Adaspace Technology (6935) opened down 1.8 percent in its IPO debut.
items.to: Nvidia stock crash weighs down on HK tech shares, Hang Seng drops below 24,000 points

items.t: Распродажа акций Гонконга продолжается: Hang Seng упал на 307 пунктов, едва защищая 24 000; Названия технических компаний пострадали сильнее всего
sum: Гонконгские акции продолжили свой слабый рост 12-го числа, при этом активные продажи в сфере технологий и интернет-компаний тянули широкий рынок вниз на протяжении всей сессии. Индекс Hang Seng закрылся на отметке 24 008,55, снизившись на 307,37 пункта, или 1,26%, зафиксировав четвертый дневной убыток подряд и едва удерживая уровень 24 000. Индекс Hang Seng Tech закрылся на отметке 3931,93, снизившись на 95,13 пункта, или на 2,36%, заметно отстав от основного рынка.

Глядя на структуру рынка, акции интернет-компаний с большой капитализацией упали практически по всем направлениям. Акции Alibaba (09988.HK) были среди голубых фишек с наихудшими показателями: в какой-то момент во время полуденной сессии они упали почти на 5%, а затем закрылись на уровне 95,6 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 12 долларов). Акции Kuaishou (01024.HK) также оказались под давлением, закрывшись на отметке 27,78 гонконгских долларов (около 3,5 долларов США), снизившись на 3,1%. JD.com (09618.HK) закрылся на уровне 107,2 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 14 долларов), снизившись на 3,5%; Tencent (00700.HK) закрылся на уровне 403,6 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 51 доллар), снизившись на 1,5%; и Meituan (03690.HK) закрылись на уровне 71,9 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 9,2 доллара), снизившись на 1,3%. Акции Xiaomi (01810.HK) держались относительно хорошо, поднявшись против тренда в полдень, а затем отступив вместе с более широким рынком в конце сессии.

Примечательно, что названия искусственного интеллекта и прикладного программного обеспечения различались. Запасы концептов больших моделей в целом упали: Zhipu резко упал, MINIMAX также снизился. Акции полупроводникового сектора, напротив, продемонстрировали устойчивость: Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) и Tianshu Zhixin (09911.HK) выросли, при этом Tianshu Zhixin выросла на 11% в полдень, а Biren Technology (06082.HK) также выросла почти на 7%. Акции SMIC (00981.HK) упали на 0,53%, указывая на то, что инвесторы придерживаются разных взглядов на полупроводники и крупные модели.

Металлы и активы-убежища одновременно ослабли, при этом акции золота и меди оказались под явным давлением. Котировки Zijin Gold International, Laopu Gold, China Nonferrous Mining (01258.HK) и China Molybdenum (03993.HK) снизились. China Molybdenum закрылась на уровне 12,18 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 1,6 доллара), снизившись на 3,7%, а Zijin Mining (02899.HK) закрылась на уровне 27,86 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 3,6 доллара), снизившись на 3,7%. Акции CK Hutchison (00001.HK) упали на 4,2% до 69,05 гонконгских долларов (приблизительно 8,8 долларов), одной из самых слабых акций тяжеловесов на тот момент.

sum: Hong Kong stocks opened lower on Wednesday as the Hang Seng Index dropped 202 points, or 0.83 percent, to 24,354, with tech majors under pressure and property counters sliding on renewed rate-hike concerns after firmer U.S. inflation data.
The Hang Seng Tech Index was down 0.96 percent to 4,045 points.

On tech majors, Alibaba (9988) plans to spin off its subsidiary T-Head for an independent listing on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, while its shares opened down 0.98 percent. Tencent (0700) fell 0.86 percent, Meituan (3690) dropped 1.06 percent, JD.com (9618) declined 0.98 percent, and Xiaomi (1810) also slipped 0.52 percent.

Among blue chips, Li Auto (2015) opened down 2.7 percent as the worst-performing blue chip. In contrast, CATL (3750) and Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor (1347) beat the market, gaining 2.6 percent and 1.6 percent respectively.

Local properties were under pressure from the potential rate hike following the US announcing the October consumer price index last night, which climbed 0.4 percent. New World Development (0016) opened down 2 percent, CK Asset (1113) fell 1.6 percent, and Henderson Land Development (0012) dropped 0.5 percent.

Separately, Link Real Estate Investment Trust (0823) opened down 0.5 percent following announcements that it will acquire a 50.1 percent interest in Eastpoint Mall in Singapore from Income Insurance for S$239.5 million (HK$1.47 billion).

sum: China's blue-chip CSI300 Index and the Shanghai Composite Index were both up 0.1% by the lunch break, while Hong Kong's benchmark Hang Seng Index gained 0.2%.

Technology stocks led gains across the region, following an overnight rally on Wall Street that saw the Nasdaq Composite jump 2.7%. China's 5G Communication Index climbed 2.7%, emerging as the best-performing sector onshore, while the technology-focused STAR50 Index advanced 1%.
Read more: Global Market Today: Asian stocks rally after US tech surge, oil slump

In Hong Kong, shares of optical communications equipment maker Zhongji Innolight surged 10%, while major technology companies listed in the city gained 0.5%, reflecting renewed investor interest in stocks linked to the artificial intelligence supply chain.

Among individual stocks, Wuxi AppTec rose as much as 5% before trimming gains after the US Pentagon removed the Chinese biotechnology company from its list of Chinese military companies. The move provided support to the company's shares amid broader gains in technology-related stocks.
Read more: US stocks: Dow rockets 1,100 points, S&P over 2% as oil slide cools inflation worries; Nvidia slumps

The gains in Chinese equities came against the backdrop of strong export performance, with the country's trade surplus exceeding $1 trillion in the first 10 months of the year. A global push to develop artificial intelligence infrastructure has boosted overseas demand for Chinese high-tech products, helping offset weakness in domestic consumption, Reuters reported.

sum: Following the sharp drop in stock prices on Wall Street, markets in East Asia got off to a positive start this trading week. (File photo)
Stock markets in East Asia have rebounded somewhat following last week's dramatic sell-off in AI sector stocks. The Japanese benchmark index, in particular, rose significantly.

At the start of the week, two hours after the market opened, Japan's leading index, the Nikkei 225, was up a solid 3 percent. At the same time (11:00 a.m. local time), South Korea's Kospi was up 1.2 percent.

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, memory chip manufacturers that play a key role in the AI supply chain, also got off to a positive start to the trading week, rising 2.6 percent and 3.7 percent, respectively.

The Hang Seng Index on the stock exchange in the Chinese Special Administrative Region of Hong Kong, which opened an hour later, rose by about 0.7 percent, while the CSI 300 Index—which tracks the 300 leading stocks on China’s mainland stock exchanges—rose by just under 0.5 percent.
At the end of last week, an extraordinary AI-driven sell-off took place on Wall Street, which also hit Asian stock markets hard.
items.to: East Asian Stock Markets Open Higher After AI-Driven Sell-Off

sum: Hong Kong shares opened lower on Friday, tracking a global tech sell-off as potential tighter artificial intelligence regulation rattled market sentiment.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index dropped 392 points, or 1.58 percent, to 24,404.
Lenovo (0992) kept slipping after logging a 6 percent loss a day ago, down 9.6 percent at the open, marking the worst performance among blue chips.

Chipmakers also dragged down the market. Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor (1347) fell 8.6 percent despite a 1.5 percent rise in third-quarter net profit released a day ago, while SMIC (0981) opened 6.4 percent lower.
Tech majors underperformed the market, with Alibaba (9988) and Tencent (0700) decreasing 3.8 percent and 2.2 percent.
In contrast, PetroChina (0857) and CNOOC (0883) went up 1.5 percent and 0.3 percent on the rebounding oil prices.

sum: The Hang Seng Index jumped 2.9%, or 702 points, to 24,618 on Thursday, extending gains for a second consecutive session and reaching a five-week high.
The rally was primarily driven by improved global risk appetite following Democratic victories in the US midterm elections, which fueled hopes of renewed efforts to end the Middle East conflict.
Brent crude plunged more than 8% to below US$95 per barrel, easing inflation concerns, while lower US Treasury yields and a weaker dollar.
Buying interest was further boosted by Wall Street’s strong rebound, with the S&P 500 rising 1.6% on Wednesday, its biggest advance in three months, while the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.9%.

Domestically, Beijing’s market-stabilization efforts reinforced sentiment, as state-backed funds directed around US$11.5 billion into nine ETFs, while applications for PBOC-backed share-buyback loans exceeded CNY200 billion.
Top gainers were Tencent (4.9%), Xiaomi (4.0%), Meituan (5.6%), Alibaba (2.6%), and AIA (2.4%).
items.to: Hong Kong Stocks Surge to Five-Week High

sum: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 0.42% to 23,393.32 on Monday 2 November 2026, its second straight gain, as the Hang Seng Tech Index surged 2.25% led by Xiaomi, CATL, Alibaba and Tencent, while banks and gold miners lagged.

The Hang Seng Index, the main benchmark of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, closed at 23,393.32 on Monday, up 98.90 points or 0.42%, according to Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing data reported by Xinhua and The Standard. It followed Friday's 1.5% rebound and marked the index's first session of November in positive territory.

The index traded as high as 23,543.30 but gave back part of those gains in the afternoon. The more significant move came in technology: the Hang Seng Tech Index jumped 2.25% to 3,839.41 after rising as much as 3% intraday, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index added 0.56% to 7,906.11. Full-day turnover reached HK$204.84 billion.

Two forces supported the market. First, expectations of fresh policy support in mainland China lifted sentiment, after regulators met banks and brokers to discuss stabilising the equity market and the People's Bank of China signalled a new liquidity operation. Chinese brokerage stocks were among the leaders as investors bet on higher trading volumes.

Second, easing oil prices and a recovery in US stock futures after Friday's technology sell-off gave investors confidence to buy back into beaten-down tech names ahead of Apple's quarterly results. Even so, the gain in the broader Hang Seng was modest because banks and gold-related stocks, which had served as havens in October, were sold to fund purchases elsewhere.

Xiaomi was the best-performing blue chip, rising 6.1%, followed closely by battery giant CATL, which gained about 6% as lithium battery shares rallied. Among the heavyweights, Alibaba climbed 2.5% and Tencent advanced 2.2%, together providing a large share of the index's points gain.

Chipmakers also recovered. Hua Hong Semiconductor rose nearly 3% and SMIC added 1.5%. Casino operators climbed despite a decline in Macao's October gaming revenue, with Galaxy Entertainment up 3.7% and Sands China up 3.1%. On the downside, Bank of China and BOC Hong Kong were among the weakest constituents after their recent results, and gold miners eased.

items.t: Регуляторы Китая поддерживают акции после октябрьского спада, сообщают материковые СМИ
sum: Chinese financial regulators are preparing to take action to stabilize the market after a sharp decline in A-shares during October, according to mainland media reports.

The reports said that the People’s Bank of China, the China Securities Regulatory Commission, and the National Financial Regulatory Administration will meet with major banks on Monday. The regulators are expected to discuss expanding capital market support tools, including optimizing special re-lending facilities for stock buybacks and share purchases.
The special re-lending facility is designed to help listed companies and major shareholders access low-cost funds to repurchase shares and bolster stock prices.
A-shares experienced a significant downturn in October, with major indices hitting new lows for the year.
The Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.44 percent to close at 3,599.00 points on the final trading day of October, dropping below the 3,600-point mark for the first time this year.

Growth and tech stocks led the slide, with the Shenzhen Component Index down 2.73 percent to 10,833.78, the ChiNext Index dropping 4.13 percent to 2,413.63, and the SSE Science and Technology Innovation Board 50 Index declining 4.66 percent to 1,421.31.

Declines were widespread across sectors, led by heavy sell-offs in tech and media shares. More than 4,600 stocks across the entire market recorded losses. Combined turnover on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges reached 1.67 trillion yuan (HK$1.97 trillion) that day, up 117.9 billion yuan from the previous session.

sum: Hong Kong stocks are currently in a significant "valuation trough" within the global financial markets.

In October 2026, the Hang Seng Index had a P/E ratio of 13.04x, with overall valuations far lower than those in the US $NASDAQ 100 Index (.NDX.US)$ (which reached as high as 29x). From a purely valuation perspective, Hong Kong stocks may appear highly attractive to investors. However, the market is well aware that "cheap" does not equate to having upward catalysts; low valuations are often intertwined with deep-seated structural issues. Nevertheless,Low valuations and high dividend yields have become reasons for investors to continue holding positions during inflationary cycles.。

After the significant pullback in October, the market is closely watching whether Hong Kong stocks will see a revenge rally in November, which is also the strong hope of many retail investors at present.However, for the broader market to truly reverse its weakness, it remains constrained by multiple complex domestic and external factors.

sum: Tech shares slumped in Asia on Friday, the yen rose and bonds surged towards their biggest monthly gain in nearly three years as investors scurried to safety against worries that huge and rising AI spending may not deliver sufficient returns.
In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 52 points, or 0.23 percent, at 23,011.
The China enterprises index rose 23 points, or 0.31 percent, to 7,779 while the tech index fell 23 points, or 0.63 percent, to 3,720.
Up north, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index opened down 45 points, or 1.25 percent, at 3,605.

The blue-chip CSI300 headed for its largest monthly fall in a decade, after nearly four months of AI stocks tanking on fears that a slowdown in demand for chips and other data centre equipment could crush revenues.
The Shenzhen Component Index fell 267 points, or 2.4 percent, to 10,871 while the ChiNext Index plunged 3.29 percent to 2,434.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 315 points, or 0.49 percent, down at 64,344 and was 1,742 points lower at one stage before noon as the tech-heavy 225 benchmark tracked overnight losses on Wall Street and was given additional impetus by late earnings from Amazon.com and Intel that showed massive cash burns.

items.t: Акции Гонконга упали в конце торгов; Индекс Hang Seng упал ниже 23 000, индекс Hang Seng Tech упал на 2,84%
sum: Hong Kong stocks traded choppily and weakened on the 29th. The Hang Seng Index rose about 90 points in early trading before selling pressure emerged, with losses widening to nearly 170 points in late trading as the 23,000 round-number level was breached again. The index ended at 22,958.65, down 136.18 points or 0.59%, with the daily candlestick turning black. The Hang Seng Tech Index fell more sharply, closing at 3,744.14, down 109.58 points or 2.84%. Main board turnover exceeded HK$189.4 billion (approximately $24.1 billion).

The correction was centered on AI and semiconductor names. Rising doubts over whether massive AI capital spending can translate into actual returns weighed on related stocks. Lenovo Group plunged 6.9% in a single session, while MINIMAX, Zhipu and Tianshu Zhixin fell 7% to 9%. Chip stocks weakened in tandem, with SMIC down nearly 6% and Hua Hong Semiconductor down more than 7%, as optical communications, memory and chip-related concept stocks came under broad pressure.

Large internet stocks were also not spared from the adjustment, with JD.com, Tencent, Meituan and Alibaba falling between nearly 2% and nearly 3%. Kuaishou and Bilibili pulled back noticeably, while Xiaomi edged higher against the trend.

Notably, capital clearly rotated out of technology names into financial and energy sectors. Ping An Insurance and PetroChina both rose nearly 3% after reporting earnings, while Chinese bank stocks advanced against the market, with the four major state-owned banks and China Merchants Bank gaining between more than 1% and more than 2%, becoming a supporting force for the broader market.

In contrast to the prior session, the Hang Seng Index had just closed up 0.23% on the 28th, and the Hang Seng Tech Index had surged 1.4%, led by storage, semiconductor and optical communications sectors. Hua Hong Semiconductor jumped more than 8% that day, and Lenovo Group also climbed more than 6%. In just one trading day, market sentiment shifted from optimism to caution, indicating that the valuation of the AI theme has entered a highly sensitive and volatile phase.

items.t: Tencent, Alibaba и Hengke отступают: рынок начинает оценивать инвестиции в ИИ по доходности
sum: Tencent, Alibaba and Hengke pull back: the market starts to price AI investments based on returns

On October 22, the Hang Seng Tech Index fell 5.03% to close at 3793.93 points. The index's trading volume reached HK$72.599 billion, up 55.9% from HK$46.56 billion in the previous trading day, marking the highest single-day level since October.
Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) fell 2.89% to close at HK$382.40; Alibaba (09988.HK) dropped 6.12% to close at HK$97.35, falling below the HK$100 threshold.

Just two days ago, the Hang Seng Tech Index was still above the 4000-point mark. Calculated from the intraday high of 6715.46 points on October 2, 2025, the Hang Seng Tech Index has retraced 43.5%. Since the beginning of this year, the Hang Seng Tech Index has fallen 31.2%, Tencent has dropped 35.4%, and Alibaba has decreased 31.2%.

In terms of capital flows, in August, Alibaba placed new shares to raise approximately HK$80 billion, which will be invested in AI capabilities and infrastructure. Tencent announced a new round of USD and RMB bond issuances in October — both companies are expanding their AI investment, however, the market has begun to "press for answers" on how previous investments can be converted into cash flow and profits at a faster pace.

At the macro level, the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note remains above 5%, and the scale of Hong Kong IPO financing has also increased significantly since the start of this year. Interest rates, corporate expenditures and stock supply are jointly changing the price that buyers are willing to pay.

The share price adjustments of Tencent and Alibaba reflect that the market has begun to recalculate the returns on AI investments. In the past, increasing investment in computing power and models was enough to support growth expectations; now, investors are more concerned about how much revenue, profit and per-share cash return new investments can bring. The Hang Seng Tech Index has fallen in tandem, and this return verification has expanded from the two companies to the entire sector.
items.to: Tencent, Alibaba & Hengke Pull Back: Market Begins Pricing AI Investments by Returns

sum: The Hang Seng Index plunged 2.9%, while Hong Kong's technology stocks dropped 4.6%. In mainland China, the blue-chip CSI300 Index fell 1.3% by the midday break, leaving it nearly 20% below its June peak. The Shanghai Composite Index declined 0.9%.
A decline of 20% or more from a recent peak is widely regarded as the threshold for a technical bear market.
Read more: Global Market Today: Asian stocks mixed as oil rally, AI concerns weigh on sentiment

According to Reuters, investor sentiment has weakened amid disappointment over Beijing's limited stimulus measures and reduced expectations for additional policy support following stronger-than-expected third-quarter economic growth.

China's measures announced ahead of the National Day holiday, including mortgage interest subsidies for first-time buyers of lower-priced properties, fell short of market expectations, Kelly Chung, chief investment officer for multi-assets at Value Partners, said.
Read more: US stocks today: Nasdaq leads Wall Street higher as SpaceX, Super Micro lift AI sentiment

Leo Wang, a partner at Beijing-based Qianchuang Capital, said investors had concentrated their holdings in technology stocks during the first half of 2026, a trend reflected in mutual fund portfolios reported for the second quarter. This concentration contributed to excessive valuations in some sectors while diverting investment away from others, Reuters reported.

sum: In the morning session on Oct. 21, China's A-share and Hong Kong markets diverged. The computing-power hardware chain rebounded collectively, with optical module, optical communication and optical chip concept stocks surging, lifting the STAR 50 index more than 1% in early trading. On the other side, power battery leader CATL (300750.SZ) fell about 9% in both its A-share and Hong Kong listings, becoming the main heavyweight dragging on the indices.

As of press time, the Shanghai Composite was down 0.07%, the Shenzhen Component was up 0.38% and the ChiNext Index was up 0.15%. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index was up 0.35% and the Hang Seng Tech Index was up 0.67%. In the bond market, Chinese government bond futures weakened across the board, with the 30-year main contract down 0.31%, while the 10-year, 5-year and 2-year main contracts fell 0.06%, 0.04% and 0.01%, respectively. Commodity futures were mixed: asphalt, Shanghai nickel, Shanghai tin and Shanghai silver rose more than 1%, while coke, Shanghai copper, lithium carbonate, rebar and iron ore advanced; soybean meal, wood pulp, glass and Shanghai gold declined, with industrial silicon, crude oil and fuel oil down more than 1%.
Computing hardware sentiment recovers, optical communications sector leads

The direct trigger for this rebound came from overnight U.S. stocks. Super Micro Computer reported quarterly results that far exceeded market expectations, and the "AI trade" warmed in response. Server makers Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise rose significantly after the bell, and AI cloud computing company CoreWeave also strengthened. Driven by this, chip stocks across Asia-Pacific rebounded broadly, with South Korea's KOSPI up more than 3% and South Korea's Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS) each up about 6%.

After the A-share open, expectations for a recovery in AI hardware spread quickly. The Shanghai Composite opened up 0.14% and the ChiNext Index up 0.28%, with optical modules and memory sectors strengthening first, while coal, agriculture, precious metals and education sectors pulled back.

items.t: Гонконгская фондовая биржа: Индекс Hang Seng упал до 23 867,74 на фоне падения цен на акции после перерыва в работе Chung Yeung
sum: Hong Kong equities returned from Monday's Chung Yeung Festival holiday with a broad decline on Tuesday 20 October 2026, as the Hang Seng absorbed two days of global news, the unchanged Chinese lending rates and a fresh sell-off in technology shares.

The Hang Seng Index closed at 23,867.74 points on Tuesday 20 October 2026, down 319.09 points or 1.32% from Friday's close of 24,186.83, according to Xinhua and RTHK data. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index fell 1.21% to 8,030.26, while the Hang Seng Tech Index dropped 1.52% to 4,045.91.

Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing kept its securities markets closed on Monday 19 October for the day following the Chung Yeung Festival, which fell on a Sunday this year. Tuesday's session was therefore the first chance for Hong Kong investors to react to China's third-quarter GDP data, Monday's rebound in US technology stocks and the People's Bank of China's loan prime rate decision.

The Hang Seng finished at 23,867.74, a loss of 1.32%, wiping out Friday's 0.52% gain. The index stayed in negative territory throughout the session, with selling pressure intensifying in the afternoon and no meaningful recovery into the close.

The close leaves the benchmark back below the psychologically important 24,000 mark. Reuters reported that the Hang Seng Tech Index touched a two-year low during the session, underlining the scale of the pressure on Hong Kong's technology sector.

Technology and financial stocks led the decline after China left its key lending rates unchanged, according to RTHK. The one-year loan prime rate stayed at 3.00% and the five-year rate at 3.50%, the 17th consecutive month without a change. Stronger-than-expected growth reduced hopes that Beijing would deliver additional stimulus.

China's economy grew 4.5% year on year in the third quarter, accelerating from 4.3% and beating the 4.4% consensus, driven largely by exports. Good news for the economy turned into bad news for markets that had been hoping for easier monetary policy. Regional weakness compounded the move, as Japan's Nikkei fell 1.30% and South Korea's KOSPI slumped 3.73% on concerns about AI spending and rising bond yields.

items.t: Гонконгская фондовая биржа сегодня: Индекс Hang Seng упал до 24 510,09, поскольку распродажа технологий углубляется в праздничных торгах
sum: The Hang Seng Index dropped 251.04 points to 24,510.09, its third straight decline, after touching a two-month low at midday as Chinese technology stocks slid and investors found little substance in the Trump-Xi summit. Mainland markets were closed for the Mid-Autumn Festival.

The Hang Seng Index closed at 24,510.09 on Friday, 25 September 2026, down 251.04 points or 1.01% from Thursday's close of 24,761.13, according to Google Finance and ME News data. The index opened at 24,523.50, already well below the previous close, reached a high of just 24,537.14, and slid to an intraday low of 24,275.56 during the morning session.

At the midday break, Reuters reported the index down 1.7% at 24,343.19, its lowest level in two months. The afternoon brought a partial recovery of more than 230 points from the low, but the benchmark still finished firmly in the red. It was the third consecutive losing session, following a 1.01% drop on Wednesday and a 0.29% decline on Thursday, and it leaves the index about 2.3% below its 22 September close of 25,087.75.

Technology shares led the declines. The Hang Seng Tech Index fell 1.13% to 4,311.78 at the close, after dropping more than 2% to a three-month low in the morning, with NetEase, Xiaomi and AAC Technologies among the notable losers, down between 1.8% and 3.05%, according to ME News. Reuters reported that AI-related stocks slid nearly 3% at one point, and the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index, which tracks mainland companies listed in the city, fell roughly 2% in the morning.

The macro trigger was the global bond sell-off. On Thursday, the US 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.225%, its highest since 2007, while the 30-year hit its highest since 2004. Higher US yields tend to pressure Hong Kong particularly hard because the city's currency peg ties local interest rates to US policy and because growth-oriented Chinese technology stocks are sensitive to the discount rate applied to future earnings.

Investors had hoped the Washington summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping would deliver a clearer framework for trade relations. Instead, Reuters described the meeting as heavy on symbolism but without apparent breakthroughs on AI, trade, Taiwan or the Iran conflict.

sum: The CSI300 Index fell 0.3% by the midday break, while the Shanghai Composite Index was little changed. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index edged up 0.2%. China's producer prices rose at their fastest pace in more than four years in September, while consumer inflation came in below market expectations. Higher oil and commodity prices pushed up factory-gate costs, but subdued domestic demand continued to limit broader inflationary pressures, the report stated.
Also Read | Global Market: China’s yuan firms as investors await US CPI data, assess inflation

Energy stocks outperformed as oil prices climbed amid concerns over potential supply disruptions involving Saudi Arabia. The Coal Index gained 1.2%, while the CSI Energy Index rose nearly 2%. Consumer staples shares also advanced, climbing 0.7%.

Technology shares remained under pressure, however, as sentiment towards companies linked to the artificial intelligence supply chain continued to deteriorate. The 5G Communication Index dropped 1.5%, while the technology-focused STAR50 Index fell 1.1%. Zhongji Innolight, a leading manufacturer of optical transceivers used in AI data centres, declined 2.6%.

Chinese stock benchmarks have struggled to sustain the rally sparked by Beijing's stimulus measures, which had raised hopes of a prolonged bull market. The recovery has since lost momentum, with the market entering a three-month downtrend and major indexes hovering near levels seen during earlier periods of weakness.
Also Read | Global Market: Japan's Nikkei rebounds as chip stocks rise, Topix slips on bank losses

Value stocks have outperformed growth shares since July, but HSBC analysts cautioned that the trend could be temporary. They pointed to relatively lower valuations among growth stocks and stronger earnings-revision momentum as factors that could support a reversal, as per the report.

sum: ASIAN stocks declined, tracking moves on Wall Street, as elevated oil prices stoked inflation concerns and technology shares came under renewed pressure.
MSCI’s Asia Pacific index for equities slipped 0.3 per cent, with shares in Japan and South Korea falling, while markets in mainland China return from a holiday.

Among the main moves across markets, S&P 500 futures were little changed as at 9.03 am Tokyo time. Hang Seng futures fell 0.6 per cent, Japan’s Topix fell 0.9 per cent and Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.4 per cent.
Shares of Samsung Electronics fluctuated between gains and losses after the chip bellwether reported record profit but still missed estimates.

Elsewhere, Brent rose 1 per cent to around US$101.20 a barrel after a report that the White House asked the Pentagon to draw up strike options against Iran that could be executed before the midterm elections, and as a storm shut some US output.

Earlier, the S&P 500 Index and the Nasdaq 100 Index both fell 0.2 per cent on renewed concerns about inflation. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 1.2 per cent. A Bloomberg gauge of the US dollar’s strength touched its highest since June in the New York session.
Higher oil prices are complicating the outlook for investors by adding to inflationary pressures just as the US Federal Reserve in September increased interest rates for the first time since 2023.

sum: Regional stocks were off to a mixed start on Monday while the US dollar edged lower and bonds steadied, as investors trimmed bets on an aggressive policy tightening cycle by the Federal Reserve following cooler-than-expected US jobs data.
Trading was thin in Asia with holidays in the Chinese mainland and South Korea, leaving markets to take their cue from Wall Street's moves on Friday.
In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened down eight points, or 0.04 percent, at 23,963.
The tech index slid 19 points, or 0.47 percent, to 4,138 while the China Enterprises Index inched nine points, or 0.12 percent, down to 8,021.

Data last week showed US job growth slowed more than expected in September and the nonfarm payrolls count for the prior two months was revised sharply lower, almost taking another rate hike from the Fed this month off the table.

"Labour conditions are stable overall, but Friday's downward revisions signal that the US economy has lost jobs in two out of the nine months year to date, and the risk of further employment losses means that the Fed can't hike another 100 basis points from here, which is what the curve is pricing in," said Jose Torres, senior economist at Interactive Brokers.
Investors are now pricing in just a 22 percent chance that the Fed could raise rates this month, as compared to a 64 percent chance a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

sum: Hong Kong stocks suffered a heavy blow on the first trading day of October, with the Hang Seng Index losing the psychologically important 24,000-point level and posting its steepest single-day decline in nearly half a year. On October 2, the benchmark index traded in a narrow range at low levels throughout the day, with intraday losses widening to as much as 3% before closing at 23,972.29, down 640.98 points or 2.6%—the largest single-day drop since the 3.54% decline on March 23. The Hang Seng Tech Index weakened in tandem, closing down 2.26% at 4,157.94, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index fell 2.31% to 8,030.54.

From a sector perspective, physical AI concepts, real estate, new energy vehicles, pharmaceuticals, and financials bore the brunt of selling pressure, while the optical communications supply chain bucked the trend and memory chip-related products also delivered notable gains.

The external pressure behind Hong Kong's sharp decline stemmed from a chain reaction in global bond markets. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since 2002, while the 30-year yield hit a 24-year high. The UK 30-year gilt yield briefly breached 6% for the first time since 1998, and Japan's 10-year government bond yield had already risen above 3% in September—the highest since 1996—demonstrating that the rise in long-end rates is not unique to the United States. Elevated long-end yields push up financing costs for financial institutions and compress asset valuations, making this the core drag on the day's trading.

A vacuum in capital flows amplified the decline. The Stock Connect southbound channel was suspended from October 1 due to the mainland China National Day holiday and will not resume until October 8. Mainland A-shares are also closed through October 7. With southbound capital absent, Hong Kong stocks lost a crucial source of incremental buying.

Pressured by surging long-end rates, international financial stocks were among the day's worst performers. AIA Group (1299.HK) fell 5.98% to HK$69.2 (approximately $8.8), hitting a near one-year low and ranking as the worst-performing blue chip of the day.

sum: Hong Kong stocks encountered broad-based selling pressure in early trading on September 25, with all three major indices opening lower and extending their declines throughout the morning session. By the midday break, the Hang Seng Index had fallen 1.69% to 24,343.19 points, while the Hang Seng Tech Index tumbled 2.14%. The Hang Seng Index had closed at 25,087.75 points on September 22, then broke below the 25,000-point threshold on September 23 to close at 24,834.12 points. The further decline by midday on September 25 brought the cumulative pullback from the September 22 close to approximately 3%. Chinese tech stocks and Chinese property developers were the two main drags on the broader market, with sentiment clearly shifting toward caution.

Large-cap Chinese tech stocks declined almost across the board. Xiaomi (01810.HK) fell more than 3%, Kuaishou (01024.HK) dropped over 3%, while Alibaba (09988.HK), Baidu (09888.HK), Meituan (03690.HK), and JD.com (09618.HK) all lost more than 2%. NetEase (09999.HK) briefly fell over 3% intraday, and Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) also weakened in sympathy.

Chinese property developers were similarly subdued, though the decline appeared to be more of a profit-taking pullback following the policy-driven rally. Sunac China (01918.HK) saw its morning decline approach 7% at one point, while China Vanke (02202.HK) and R&F Properties (02777.HK) fell over 5%, and Longfor Group (00960.HK) and Country Garden (02007.HK) dropped nearly 5%. Another Chinese property developer, Ronshine China (03301.HK), plunged more than 14% at one point, indicating strong selling appetite in the real estate sector. Just four trading days earlier, on September 21, Chinese property stocks had surged collectively, with Sunac China gaining over 10% and China Vanke rising more than 7% that day. The catalyst for that rally was a package of real estate policy documents jointly issued on August 28 by five Chinese government bodies—the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Ministry of Natural Resources, the People's Bank of China, the National Financial Regulatory Administration, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission—covering commercial housing sales management, real estate credit rules, and capital market financing for property developers.

sum: Hong Kong shares finished at the high of the day on 21 September 2026, extending Friday's rebound as investors bet on a constructive Trump-Xi summit, a Beijing drug-industry plan and lower oil prices.

The Hang Seng Index, the benchmark of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, closed Monday at 25,042.71, a gain of 291.93 points or 1.18% from Friday's close of 24,750.78. The index opened at 24,748.45, only marginally lower than the previous close, and reached its low of 24,736.92 in the opening minutes. From there it climbed for most of the day, and it finished at the session high, meaning that buyers held control right through the closing auction. Turnover was about HK$202.7 billion, a healthy figure that supports the view that the advance had genuine participation behind it.

The gain extended a two-day recovery. The index had closed at 24,604.29 on Thursday, the day after the Federal Reserve's rate increase, and then gained 0.6% on Friday to 24,750.78. With Monday's advance the benchmark is back above the psychologically important 25,000 mark, a level it had slipped below earlier this month.

Three forces combined. The first was diplomacy. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said weekend talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng were very successful, and the discussions touched on trade and artificial intelligence. Reports also indicated that the two sides have been discussing reciprocal tariff reductions on about $30 billion of goods each, and that Washington may hold back new tariff announcements until after the summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, which is scheduled for 24 September. For Hong Kong, where many of the largest listed companies depend on Chinese consumers and on global trade, that kind of tone is very supportive.

The second force was domestic policy. On 18 September, ten Chinese government departments, including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the National Development and Reform Commission, issued a five-year development plan for the pharmaceutical industry, with targets that include average annual growth of at least 20% in the innovative drug sector by 2030. Pharmaceutical and biotechnology shares led Monday's gains, and exchange-traded funds tracking Hong Kong innovative drug companies rose about 6%.

items.t: Crealights официально включена в Stock Connect, новую веху на рынке капитала для пионера AI Silicon Photonics Interconnect
sum: HONG KONG, Sept 7, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - Crealights Technology Co., Ltd. ('Crealights' or the 'Company', Stock Code: 1191.HK) has been officially included as a constituent stock of the Hang Seng Composite Index, becoming eligible for the Stock Connect trading scheme starting today. Mainland investors can now trade the Company's shares directly through the Stock Connect channels, which is expected to further broaden the Company's investor base and enhance its share trading liquidity.

This inclusion follows the Hang Seng Index Company's quarterly review results for the period ended June 30, 2026, announced on August 21, 2026. The inclusion deepens the Company's connection with the onshore capital market, which is expected to attract greater long-term capital interest and provide more diversified capital market support for the Company's long-term value growth.
Continuous Financial Deliverables and Accelerated Product Structure Upgrades

The Company released its post-listing interim results on August 28. During the reporting period, total revenue reached RMB798.5 million, representing a year-on-year increase of 14.4% and a half-on-half growth of 52.7%. The revenue contribution from silicon photonics products surged significantly from 15.3% in the same period last year to 39.0%, as the Company's business structure continues to upgrade toward higher-speed and higher-value-added solutions.

With 800G silicon photonics modules entering the volume shipment stage-supporting maximum transmission distances of up to approximately two kilometers-the Company's large-scale commercial application capabilities in silicon photonics technology have been further validated. During the reporting period, R&D expenses increased by 58.5% year-on-year to RMB67.8 million, raising its proportion of total revenue to 8.5%. These investments were primarily channeled into continuous R&D for high-speed optical interconnects and next-generation silicon photonics products, securing technical reserves for subsequent product iteration and commercialization.
Multi-Dimensional Growth Drivers to Capture Long-Cycle AI Infrastructure Dividends
The accelerated construction of AI data centers has driven a sustained surge in demand for high-speed optical interconnects.
items.to: Crealights Officially Included in Stock Connect, A New Capital Market Milestone for the AI Silicon Photonics Interconnect Pioneer

sum: Hong Kong stocks rallied at the open on Friday, as US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller's comments eased interest rate hike concerns.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index rose 302 points, or 1.2 percent, to 25,515.
With gold prices climbing back to surpass US$4,500 (HK$35,100), Zijin Ming (2899) jumped 4 percent at the open, marking the best performer among blue chips. Laopu Gold was also up 2.4 percent.
Tech giants outperformed the market. Alibaba (9988) and Tencent (0700) advanced 1.9 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively.
Lenovo (0992) ascended 3.2 percent, while JD.com (9618) and Baidu (9888) both rose 2.5 percent.
Notably, Chinese artificial intelligence firm MiniMax (0100) increased 2.7 percent, and its rival Z.AI (2513) grew by 1.4 percent.

sum: Hong Kong stocks erased early gains to close lower on Thursday, while biopharmaceutical stocks outperformed the market.
The benchmark Hang Seng Index fell 97 points, or 0.39 percent, to 25,213. The full-day turnover hit a nearly four-month low at HK$199.3 billion.
The Hang Seng Tech Index dropped 1.08 percent to 4,468 points.
Sino Biopharmaceutical (1177) surged 6.3 percent, marking the best performance among blue chips.
Its peers CSPC Pharmaceutical (1093), WuXi Biologics (2269), and Hansoh Pharmaceutical (3692) also gained 4.8 percent, 3 percent, and 2.4 percent, respectively.
Developers China Resources Land (1109) and China Overseas Land & Investment (0688) advanced 3.5 percent and 2.3 percent.
However, Trip.com (9961) led the decline among HSI constituents, slumping 5.4 percent at the close.

sum: Hong Kong stocks started September under pressure, with the Hang Seng Index falling 1.1% to around 25,307 in early trading on Tuesday. Rising oil prices amid renewed tensions between the US and Iran weighed on investor sentiment and raised concerns that higher energy costs could fuel inflation. The decline came despite signs of improving activity in China’s private manufacturing sector. The RatingDog Manufacturing PMI rose to 51.5 in August from 50.9 in July, indicating stronger expansion.

The latest weakness was largely linked to developments in the Middle East. Rising risks around the Strait of Hormuz pushed crude prices higher, increasing concerns that prolonged energy disruptions could add to global inflation. Investors are also assessing the possibility of further monetary tightening in the US if inflation remains elevated. The Hang Seng Index briefly moved below its 100-day moving average, while the Hang Seng Tech Index declined around 1.19%.

Shein had a weak debut on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, with its shares falling more than 9% shortly after trading began. The company raised approximately HK$13.6 billion through its initial public offering at HK$48.56 per share, giving it a valuation of about US$26.5 billion. The weak debut added to pressure across the broader market.
However, Kuaishou bucked the broader trend, gaining more than 6% after announcing the integration of its AI assets into its Beijing operations.

The market decline came despite improved private-sector manufacturing data from China. The RatingDog Manufacturing PMI climbed to 51.5 in August, up from 50.9 in July. The reading indicates that factory activity expanded at a faster pace, providing some support to the outlook for China’s economy. However, concerns surrounding the property sector and renewed geopolitical tensions continued to weigh on investor confidence.

sum: Hong Kong equities opened the week on a weaker note, with the three major indices falling during Monday’s morning session. The Hang Seng Index declined 0.71%, while the Hang Seng TECH Index fell 1.03% and the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index slipped 0.30%. By midday, 660 stocks had gained, 1,489 declined and 1,129 remained unchanged.

Technology shares mostly moved lower. SenseTime-W fell 4.39%, Tencent dropped 1.41%, Baidu Group-SW declined 1.36% and Kuaishou-W lost 1.32%. Xiaomi Group-W fell 0.79%, Alibaba-W declined 0.61% and NetEase slipped 0.21%. Meituan-W was among the few gainers, rising 1.16%.

Gold-related shares saw sharp declines after spot gold briefly dropped below $4,400 following a more hawkish stance from the US Federal Reserve. Tongguan Gold plunged 10.96%, Chifeng Gold fell 9.45%, Lingbao Gold dropped 9.12% and China Gold International declined 8.19%. Zijin Mining lost 5.59%, while Shandong Gold gained 3.53%. Nonferrous metal stocks also weakened, with Luoyang Molybdenum down 6.67%, Jiangxi Copper falling 6.61% and China Hongqiao declining 3.91%.

Most major automobile stocks traded in the red. BYD fell 6.69%, Leapmotor declined 6.54% and Nio-SW dropped 3.24%. Geely Auto lost 2.93%, XPeng Group-W fell 2.14%, Great Wall Motor declined 1.76% and Li Auto-W dropped 1.71%.

Property developers also faced selling pressure. China Jinmao plunged 14.65%, Greentown China fell 12.84% and China Resources Land declined 7.72%. Longfor Group dropped 6.70%, China Overseas Development fell 6.44% and Sunac China lost 5.19%. Hong Kong retail stocks were similarly weak, with Luk Fook Group down 8.38%, Chow Sang Sang falling 7.24% and Chow Tai Fook declining 6.91%.

Domestic Chinese bank stocks moved higher across the board. Postal Savings Bank of China surged more than 7% following its earnings announcement, while Harbin Bank gained nearly 7%. Bank of China climbed more than 5% to a new high, while China Minsheng Banking Corp. rose over 4%. Bank of Communications gained nearly 4%, with China Construction Bank and Bank of China Hong Kong both advancing more than 3%.
The gains came after major state-owned banks reported stronger interim results, with signs that pressure on net interest margins may be easing.

sum: Asian stocks mostly edged higher on Friday as investors assessed the US Treasury's move to push down long-term bond yields while analysts warned that alone would not be enough to keep borrowing costs from spiking.
In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 109 points, or 0.42 percent, at 25,807.
The China Enterprises Index rose 31 points, or 0.37 percent, to 8,579 while the tech index inched up nine points, or 0.21 percent, to 4,710.
Across the border, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index opened down 12 points, or 0.32 percent, at 3,891.
The Shenzhen Component Index slid 37 points, or 0.27 percent, lower to 13,935 while the ChiNext Index was flat at 3,495.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 789 points, or 1.19 percent, down at 65,427 before clawing back losses to hover 271 points, or 0.41 percent, at 65,945 at one stage before the midday mark.
In Seoul, the Kospi rebounded to be 52 points, or 0.77 percent, up at 6,905 after opening 92 points, or 1.35 percent, lower at 6,759.

sum: Hong Kong's stock market experienced violent turbulence on July 22, with the technology sector becoming the hardest-hit area. The Hang Seng Tech Index tumbled more than 3%, while gold and resource stocks surged against the trend, driven by escalating geopolitical risks and heightened risk-aversion sentiment, creating an extremely pronounced market divergence.

At the close, the Hang Seng Index settled at 24,892 points, down 239 points or 0.95%, losing the 25,000-point threshold. Full-day turnover reached HK$312.76 billion (approximately $39.9 billion). The China Enterprises Index also weakened, closing at 8,251 points, down 1.31%. The worst performer was the Hang Seng Tech Index, which plunged 146 points or 3.04% to 4,668 points.

Heavyweight tech stocks faced broad-based selling, becoming the primary drag on the broader market. Market reports indicated that Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) and NetEase (09999.HK) suffered severe blows, with single-day declines exceeding 7%. Tencent Holdings closed down 7.05%, with analysts attributing this closely to sector rotation. Data showed that Tencent was the most heavily reduced stock by mainland China's public funds in the previous quarter. NetEase tumbled 7.39%.

Other internet giants were not spared. Kuaishou (01024.HK) plunged 5.32%, while Bilibili dropped more than 4%. Alibaba (09988.HK), Xiaomi (01810.HK), Baidu (09888.HK), and JD.com (09618.HK) all recorded declines exceeding 2%, reflecting a heavy bearish market atmosphere.

Artificial intelligence and large model concept stocks also faced a cold spell. The previously sought-after duo, Minimax (00100.HK) and Zhipu (02513.HK), both retreated. Minimax crashed 11.42% for the day, while Zhipu pulled back after surging nearly 37% the previous day, closing down 3.61%. Reports indicated that JPMorgan recently issued a note stating that Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 had reshaped the valuation framework for large models, consequently lowering Zhipu's target price to 1,600 yuan, which exerted some pressure on market sentiment.

Semiconductor and chip stocks also mostly declined. SG Micro dropped more than 11%, APT Electronics fell over 10%, GigaDevice (03986.HK) and Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347.HK) both declined more than 4%, and bellwether SMIC (00981.HK) also reversed to fall 3.44%.

sum: Hang Seng Index Today (July 17): Hong Kong’s stock market witnessed heavy selling pressure on Friday, July 17, as technology and AI stocks faced a sharp decline amid a global market selloff. The benchmark Hang Seng Index dropped more than 400 points as investors turned cautious over stretched AI valuations, inflation concerns and uncertainty around future technology growth.

The index briefly fell over 600 points during the trading session before recovering some losses. The decline came mainly from technology and semiconductor stocks, with AI focused comapnaies witnessign some of the biggest falls. Meanwhile, mainland Chinese markets also ended lower as broader investor sentiment weakened across Asia.

The Hang Seng Index declined on Friday due to a broad-based selloff in technology and AI-related stocks. Investors reduced their exposure to high-growth companies after concerns increased over whether massive artificial intelligence investments would generate expected returns.

The weakness followed a global technology downturn, where semiconductor and AI stocks faced heavy selling pressure. Rising inflation concerns and uncertainty over interest rate policies also pushed investors toward safer assets.
Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower on Friday, with the benchmark Hang Seng Index falling 446 points, or 1.8%, to close at 24,562.
The index declined more than 600 points at one stage before recovering slightly toward the end of the session. Trading activity remained strong, with total market turnover reaching HK$322.9 billion.
The decline reflected widespread weakness across technology, AI, and semiconductor shares, which led the market downturn.

sum: Hong Kong's three major stock indexes extended their strong rally on Wednesday (16th), with the Hang Seng Index closing above the 25,000-point mark, hitting a recent high. Amid cooling US inflation data and diminishing expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes, large-cap tech and auto stocks led the charge upward, while the semiconductor sector was battered by multiple headwinds, becoming the session's biggest loser.

The Hang Seng Index opened 143 points higher and climbed steadily throughout the session, at one point surging 540 points to an intraday high of 25,221. The gains narrowed slightly by the close, finishing up 327 points, or 1.33%, at 25,008. Market turnover was robust, reaching HK$322.89 billion (approximately $41.2 billion). The Hang Seng Tech Index also strengthened, rising 93 points, or 1.98%, to 4,834, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index gained 133 points, or 1.63%, to 8,318.

Following the release of US data showing a slowdown in the year-over-year growth of the June Producer Price Index (PPI), which combined with a previously lower-than-expected Consumer Price Index (CPI), market bets on a July rate hike by the Federal Reserve have shrunk significantly. This prompted capital to flow back into risk assets, stabilizing US tech stocks and injecting upward momentum into the Hong Kong market.

Large-cap tech stocks were the main engine for the day's broad market advance. Xiaomi Corp-W (01810.HK) led the charge, soaring 6.34%. News emerged that the company's self-developed MiMo on-device model has successfully passed the filing review for China's national large language model registry, marking another step forward in its artificial intelligence strategy. Meituan-W (03690.HK) and Kuaishou-W (01024.HK) both rose over 4%, Tencent (00700.HK) gained 2.11%, and Alibaba-W (09988.HK) closed 3.09% higher.

Commenting on the tech rebound, Goldman Sachs believes that Hong Kong's internet sector has entered a critical observation period following a valuation correction. If the earnings of relevant listed companies continue to recover in the coming quarters, there is an opportunity for a strong earnings-driven recovery rally.

sum: Hong Kong's stock market rose for a fourth straight session on July 15. The Hang Seng Index closed at 24,681.10, up 340.37 points, or 1.39%, from the previous day. The advance was driven by spillover momentum from Wall Street's gains in the prior session, coupled with buying concentrated in China consumer-related stocks amid expectations of economic stimulus measures from Chinese authorities.

Among major names, internet services giant Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) posted substantial gains. E-commerce leader Alibaba Group (9988.HK) and food delivery platform Meituan (3690.HK) also finished higher. Toy maker Pop Mart (9992.HK) was also bought, highlighting the strength across China consumer-related names.

Trading got off to a firm start in the morning session. The Hang Seng Index opened at 24,551.34, up 210.61 points, or 0.86%, from the prior close. Investor sentiment improved as the market carried forward the positive momentum from Wall Street, where major stock indexes had risen in the previous session. From the opening bell, buying was concentrated in major China tech stocks, led by Tencent Holdings and Alibaba Group.

Market participants noted that expectations for consumer stimulus measures to be rolled out by the Chinese government have once again come into focus. Even amid a prolonged global monetary tightening cycle, positioning for a recovery in China's consumer spending has driven capital inflows into China consumer-related stocks listed in Hong Kong.

With this fourth consecutive session of gains, the Hang Seng Index closed decisively above the key 24,500 threshold. The combination of positive catalysts from the U.S. and policy expectations in China spurred buying across a broad range of stocks.

sum: Hong Kong's stock market rebounded sharply on July 8. Overseas investors actively bought beaten-down mainland Chinese tech stocks on dips. The Hang Seng Index closed at 24,199.46, up 702.57 points, or 2.99%, reclaiming the 24,000 level for the first time in roughly three weeks since June 17. The Hang Seng Tech Index surged 5%, with most constituent stocks advancing.

Among individual stocks, e-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding soared 12.2%, its biggest single-day gain since September 2025. Knowledge Atlas Technology, a mapping and data services company, rose more than 13% despite the expiration of its stock lock-up period.

Market participants noted that the day's rally in Hong Kong partly reflected a capital shift following a sharp sell-off in semiconductor-related stocks in markets such as South Korea. The move represented a wave of buybacks in relatively lagging mainland Chinese tech names. Reports that Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek is developing its own semiconductors also spurred buying in related stocks.

Mainland China's market, however, painted a contrasting picture. The Shanghai Composite Index fell 19.355 points, or 0.49%, to 3,970.879, extending losses to hit a roughly one-month low. The CSI 300 Index dropped 36.729 points, or 0.77%, to 4,755.534, breaching the key 4,800 level.

In mainland China's market, semiconductor stocks rose 2% and AI-related stocks gained 1.4%, mirroring Hong Kong's tech strength. However, new energy vehicle (NEV) stocks, rare earth stocks, and defense stocks tumbled between 2.8% and 5.3%, dragging down the broader market.
Closing levels for key Hong Kong and mainland China indices are as follows:

Buying was broad-based among Hang Seng Index constituents, led by tech companies. Alibaba's surge provided a significant boost to the index, while internet services and software-related stocks also advanced. "Capital shifted into mainland Chinese tech following the semiconductor plunge in the South Korean market," one market participant noted.

sum: Shanghai's stock market rebounded on the morning of July 8, reversing the previous day's losses. The Shanghai Composite Index ended the morning session at 4,011.0516, up 20.8163 points, or 0.52%, reclaiming the psychologically important 4,000 level. Semiconductor-related stocks led the charge, with shares of Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), China's largest foundry, surging as much as 7% intraday and boosting overall market sentiment.

On July 7, a sharp sell-off in South Korean semiconductor stocks spilled over into the Hong Kong market, sending the Hang Seng Index lower after three consecutive sessions of gains. SMIC was also heavily sold off during that session. However, when Shanghai opened the following day, active bargain-hunting emerged, driven by expectations for the localization of China's domestic semiconductor production. The fact that the index had fallen to a roughly one-month low the previous day also encouraged dip-buying.

In Hong Kong on July 7, the tech rout originating in South Korea chilled investor sentiment, with the Hang Seng Index closing down 119.43 points, or 0.50%, at 23,496.89. While the market briefly turned positive in early trading, sentiment deteriorated as the decline in South Korean semiconductor stocks deepened. Profit-taking spread across previously favored mainland-linked hardware tech names, including SMIC and Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL), the world's largest manufacturer of electric vehicle batteries.

In Shanghai, the previous day's decline in Hong Kong paradoxically created a sense of relative value, drawing inflows from domestic investors. As Chinese authorities position improving semiconductor self-sufficiency as a national strategy, SMIC is once again attracting attention as a core player in that effort. This suggests that, amid heightened geopolitical risks, capital flows themed around import substitution are acting as a cushion against short-term deterioration in the external environment.
Behind the slump in South Korean semiconductor stocks lie concerns over the global supply-demand balance and the impact of export controls amid intensifying U.S.-China tensions.

sum: China's A-share market displayed significant structural divergence during the morning session on July 7. While the three major indices declined collectively—with the Shanghai Composite Index briefly extending its intraday loss to 1%—the STAR Board, represented by the semiconductor supply chain, showed robust strength, with the STAR 50 Index rallying over 1% against the trend. Meanwhile, sentiment in the Hong Kong market warmed up, with the Hang Seng Tech Index surging more than 2% driven by large-cap internet stocks, forming a stark contrast with the weakness in traditional heavyweight sectors on the A-share market.

Near the midday close, the core market indices stood as follows: the Shanghai Composite fell 0.89%, the Shenzhen Component dropped 0.70%, and the ChiNext Index declined 0.60%. The Shanghai Composite briefly touched a 1% loss around 10:34 AM, while the ChiNext Index turned negative after a brief early-session spike into positive territory, with its loss reaching 0.9% at one point. Petrochemical, shipping, pharmaceutical, and precious metals sectors were the primary drags on the broader market.

In stark contrast to the weakness on the main board, the STAR 50 Index surged over 1% against the trend, with the semiconductor supply chain becoming the core focus of capital inflows. Sub-sectors including semiconductor silicon wafers, ASIC chips, and the broader semiconductor industry all saw significant rallies. Meanwhile, concept stocks such as lab-grown diamonds and online gaming were also active, while cyclical sectors like coal and petrochemicals fell into correction.

In Hong Kong, the market opened lower but staged a strong recovery. The Hang Seng Index opened down 0.2%, and the Hang Seng Tech Index opened 0.37% lower, but both quickly recovered lost ground and pushed aggressively higher. The Hang Seng Tech Index surged more than 2% intraday, with large-cap internet stocks leading the rebound. Meituan (03690.HK) rallied over 7% at one point, Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) gained more than 5%, and stocks such as Xiaomi Corporation (01810.HK), Lenovo Group (00992.HK), and Li Auto (02015.HK) all rose over 3%.

items.t: CICC заявляет, что акции Гонконга находятся на «перемежающемся минимуме»: акции Hang Seng Tech упали более чем на 33%, оценки падают, но нет политического катализатора
sum: The first half of 2026 saw Hong Kong stocks continue to face pressure amid a global market polarized between "AI and non-AI" plays. CICC's latest research report argues that the weakness in Hong Kong stocks is not accidental but a direct reflection of the "weaker consumption side of the K-shaped economy," further compounded by a structural mismatch in the tech sector and a "tight balance" caused by constrained liquidity. As of press time, the Hong Kong market has been in a downtrend for nearly nine months since early October last year, with the pullback exceeding 30%, and the internet sector plunging more than 40%.

CICC further points out that the current state of Hong Kong stocks is more of an "intermittent low" rather than a "major bottom" in the historical sense. Judging by the magnitude of the correction and valuations, the Hang Seng Tech Index has pulled back significantly, with some heavyweight stocks' valuations nearing extremes. However, from the perspective of earnings "capitulation," capital flows, and sentiment structure, the market still lacks a "policy bottom" catalyst of the same force seen at historical pivotal lows. The report provides a base-case judgment: if earnings grow 3%-4% and US Treasury yields edge lower, the Hang Seng Index (HSI) central range would be between 26,000 and 27,000 points, remaining largely range-bound, with upside dependent on a policy pivot.
Why Hong Kong Stocks Are Weak: Credit Cycle Turns Soft, Compounded by Structural Mismatch

CICC believes that the performance of Hong Kong stocks in 2026 is highly correlated with the global market's "tech theme," but the index composition of the Hong Kong market dictates a higher sensitivity to macro consumption. The report notes that the composition of Hong Kong's benchmark indices is closely tied to China's overall consumption, and this holds true even for the Hang Seng Tech Index: internet, e-commerce, new energy vehicles (NEVs), and new consumption sectors collectively account for over 70%, while the weighting of AI-related hardware tech is relatively small. Even though large model companies and some A-to-H share conversion companies have recently been included in the index, they remain at low weightings and were added relatively late.

sum: HONG KONG: Chinese stocks fell to a three-week low on Thursday, dragged down by a sharp selloff in chipmakers. Hong Kong shares rebounded on a recovery in internet heavyweights.
** China's blue-chip CSI300 Index dipped 3% to the lowest level since June 12. The Shanghai Composite Index lost 2%.
** The tech-focused Star 50 Index lost 7.7%, the biggest single-day decline since April 2025, to slip from a record high.
** The CSI Semiconductor Index also retreated from an all-time peak, plunging 9.4% in its biggest one-day decline in nearlyfour years. The index has surged nearly 110% so far this year.

** Chipmaker Naura snapped a 10-day rally that had powered it to record highs, tumbling by the daily 10% trading limit. Peers, including SMIC, Giga Device , and Hua Hong Semiconductor, declined by 6.7% to 10%.
** The banking indexes bucked broader weakness, adding 1.2%.
** "Technology stocks cooled sharply as markets underwent a period of rotation," analysts at Huatai Futures said in a note.

The Hang Seng Index rose 0.6 percent to 23,482.58 by 9.33am, according to a report from the South China Morning Post. In Asian trading, South Korea's Kospi index was a focal point due to high volatility. The index rebounded more than 4 percent after a 10 percent drop on Tuesday that had triggered a circuit breaker. Japan's Nikkei 225 was little changed.

Investors are now awaiting earnings results from US memory chipmaker Micron Technology, due later on Wednesday. The results are expected to provide insight into whether the pace of artificial intelligence infrastructure investment remains strong enough to sustain stock market momentum.

sum: Singapore – A sell-off cascaded across global markets as investors turned jittery about high-flying tech stocks and frothy valuations, with South Korea’s Kospi Index plunging 10 per cent from a record high.

Memory stocks, many of which are riding triple-digit gains in 2026, recorded some of the steepest losses, and SpaceX was poised to fall below its first-day opening price of US$150. Nasdaq 100 futures plunged 3 per cent, while those for the S&P 500 slid 1.5 per cent.

In Seoul, chip giants SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics slumped more than 12 per cent. Intel and memory chipmaker Micron Technology led a broader decline among chipmakers in US premarket trading, while SpaceX fell 4.5 per cent. Chinese equities in Hong Kong entered a bear market.

The June 23 selldown in chipmakers, among the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial-intelligence trade, comes a day after a retreat from hyperscalers such as Alphabet as investors question whether future returns can justify current spending.
Attention is now shifting to Micron’s quarterly results on June 24 after the stock rallied more than 300 per cent since January.

“Since the start of the Iran war, tech has been the only sector where institutions have increased holdings, so some volatility and profit-taking should not come as a surprise,” said Marija Veitmane, head of equity research at State Street Markets.

Brent, meanwhile, fell for a second straight day, trading 0.6 per cent lower at US$77.40 a barrel. Traders are taking comfort from signs that talks toward a permanent deal between the US and Iran got off to a hopeful start, with Washington issuing a 60-day licence allowing Tehran to sell oil on the international market.

sum: The Indian stock market benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty 50, are expected to open higher on Monday, following mixed cues from global markets, amid progress in the US-Iran peace talks, but rising crude oil prices and bond yields increased risks of higher inflation and US interest rate hike.
Asian markets traded mostly higher, while the US stock futures declined, as investors monitor latest developments in the US-Iran peace talks.
On Friday, the Indian stock market ended lower, snapping its five-session winning streak, amid a sharp selloff in information technology stocks.
The Sensex declined 607.08 points, or 0.78%, to close at 76,802.90, while the Nifty 50 settled 154.90 points, or 0.64%, lower at 24,013.10.

“Given the prevailing mixed setup, we continue to advocate a stock-specific approach, favouring relative outperformers while maintaining disciplined risk management,” said Ajit Mishra – SVP, Research, Religare Broking Ltd.

Asian markets traded higher on Monday on progress over the US-Iran peace talks. Japan’s Nikkei 225 rallied 1.75% while the Topix gained 1.17%. South Korea’s Kospi surged 1.54%, while the Kosdaq declined 0.57%. Hong Kong Hang Seng index futures indicated a lower opening. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.4%.
Gift Nifty was trading around 24,154 level, a premium of nearly 97 points from the Nifty futures’ previous close, indicating a positive start for the Indian stock market indices.

sum: Oil prices have dropped following the United States and Iran’s signing of an interim peace agreement, resuming a slide interrupted by US President Donald Trump’s warning that he could restart his military campaign.
Brent crude fell 2.3 percent on Thursday in Asia, returning the international benchmark to near to where it was 24 hours previously.
Brent futures for delivery in August stood at $77.73 as of 05:30 GMT, only about 7 percent higher than before the US and Israel launched their war on Iran on February 28.
After several days of declines, Brent briefly spiked above $81 a barrel on Wednesday after Trump warned that the US could “go right back to dropping bombs” on Iran if it doesn’t “behave”.
Shrugging off losses on Wall Street overnight, Asian stock markets rallied on renewed optimism for an end to nearly four months of disruption to global energy supply chains.
Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 and South Korea’s Kospi both hit all-time highs, gaining more than 2 percent and 1.7 percent, respectively.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index bucked the trend, dropping 1.7 percent.

items.t: Рынок Гонконга сталкивается с давлением, поскольку в июле истекает срок действия заблокированных акций на сумму 255 миллиардов гонконгских долларов.
sum: The potential wave of selling poses an additional headwind for the city’s struggling equity market
[HONG KONG] Hong Kong’s underperforming stock market may come under renewed pressure as a large amount of shares frozen under restrictions tied to equities offerings become tradable next month.

At least HK$255 billion (S$41.8 billion) worth of stocks, either from initial public offerings or secondary share sales, will see their temporary lockups expire in July, the most for any month through the rest of this year, according to exchange data calculated by Bloomberg.

Separately, Goldman Sachs Group estimates that IPO-induced lockup expiries in the city will total US$274 billion in the coming year, marking a record for any 12-month period. Shares held by cornerstone investors of a Hong Kong IPO and existing shareholders won’t be available for public trading for a period of time, typically for six months or a year after the stock’s listing.

The looming expiries result from an IPO boom in the financial hub late last year and early this year, when technology firms rushed to capture the artificial intelligence investment frenzy. The potential selling pressure would be an extra headwind for Hong Kong stocks, which have lagged Asian peers such as South Korea and Taiwan that have led the global AI trade.

Pressured by China’s struggling economy and doubts on Chinese firms’ heavy AI spending, the city’s Hang Seng Index has fallen 3 per cent this year, versus an over 100 per cent surge for Korea’s Kospi gauge and the 57 per cent gain for Taiwan’s Taiex benchmark.

“Historical precedents suggest that equities typically experience moderate downward price pressure following lock-up expiration,” Goldman analysts including Si Fu wrote in a note dated on Jun 14. Such stocks tend to see a median decline of 4 per cent in three months and 7 per cent in six months after they become tradable, they added.
items.to: Hong Kong market faces pressure as HK$255 billion in locked shares expire in July

sum: New Delhi: In a significant development, the stock market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty surged in early trade on Monday, mirroring a rally in global equities and a sharp decline in crude oil prices, after the US and Iran finalised a deal to end their 107-day war.

The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 1,112.70 points to 76,648.74 in early deals. The 50-share NSE Nifty surged 335.55 points to 23,956.40. The US and Iran finalised a deal to end their 107-day war and open the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway used to ferry one-fifth of the global oil supplies, on Friday after an in-person signing of the agreement in Switzerland.

US President Donald Trump made the announcement on Truth Social on Sunday evening, easing pressure on the global energy markets, as officials said the peace agreement would be signed on June 19 in Switzerland.

From the 30-Sensex firms, InterGlobe Aviation, Eternal, Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv, UltraTech Cement, and Larsen & Toubro were among the major winners. Sun Pharma emerged as the only laggard from the blue-chip pack. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, dropped 4.55 per cent to USD 83.36 per barrel.

In Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi jumped nearly 6 per cent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 index climbed more than 5 per cent. Shanghai’s SSE Composite index and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index were also quoting higher.
Amid the strong rally in the stock market, all 30 large-cap stocks in the BSE LargeCap index opened in the green. The biggest gains were seen in:
These stocks emerged as the top performers in early trading as investor sentiment turned sharply positive following the easing of geopolitical tensions.

sum: Asia-Pacific markets rose Wednesday, with Japan's Nikkei 225 hitting a record high, as investors appeared to look past uncertainty over U.S.-Iran negotiations aimed at ending the Middle East conflict.
Tensions have escalated between Washington and Tehran, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying on Tuesday that Iran has mined "large segments" of the Strait of Hormuz.

"They're firing on commercial ships and they've mined large segments of Hormuz — international waters," Rubio told the Senate Foreign Relations Committee. This marks his first appearance before Congress since the Iran war on Feb. 28.
A White House official told CNBC that the Pentagon has destroyed numerous mines and over 40 minelaying vessels.
The Strait of Hormuz is a critical waterway, particularly for the energy market globally — around 20% of the world's oil supplies passed through the strait before the war.
Japan's Nikkei 225 ended Wednesday's trading session 2.50% higher at 68,402.13, while the Topix added 1.83% at 3,996.20.
Mainland China's CSI 300 rose 0.49% to 4,938.81, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng was down1.62% in its last hour of trade.
